title: Advanced Serialization
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of advanced serialization using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates advanced serialization.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Advanced Serialization** as part of **Serialization, Networking, and Application Integration**. Serialization converts values to a defined external format; Kotlin serialization needs its plugin and format library, and untrusted input still requires validation. Use the subtopics—Custom Serializers, Polymorphic Serialization, Serialization Compatibility and Versioning—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Serialization converts values to a defined external format; Kotlin serialization needs its plugin and format library, and untrusted input still requires validation.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with custom serializers. Then compare it with polymorphic serialization. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Custom Serializers
items.text: Custom Serializers is one part of advanced serialization. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Polymorphic Serialization
items.text: Polymorphic Serialization crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

items.title: Serialization Compatibility and Versioning
items.text: Serialization Compatibility and Versioning means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run in the project that declares the necessary JVM, coroutine, networking, database, or serialization dependencies. Never commit real secrets.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Parsing external JSON makes its values trustworthy without validation.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
